section: Trends in India's national income, per capita income and sectoral shares; inter-state GSDP comparison
subsections: Sectoral share of GVA - at Independence vs now
Real GDP growth - recent years, trend, size since 1991
Per capita income - formula, latest all-India figure, growth

India's GDP rank - nominal and PPP, IMF projections, USD 5 trillion

accepted.s: At the time of Independence, which sector was the largest contributor to India's GDP?
accepted.x: Agriculture was the largest contributor to India's GDP at the time of Independence.
accepted.tq: Use the historical sectoral-position contrast.
accepted.sec: Sectoral share of GVA - at Independence vs now  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Industry accounted for approximately what share of India's GDP in 1950-51?
accepted.x: Industry contributed about 13 percent of GDP in 1950-51.
accepted.tq: Recall the precise historical percentage.
accepted.sec: Sectoral share of GVA - at Independence vs now  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the changing sectoral composition of India's economy:
1. Agriculture's share had declined to about 17 percent by 2017-18.
2. Services account for more than 50 percent of GDP in the present structure.
3. The present order of sectoral contribution is services, industry and agriculture.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: agriculture's share was about 17 percent by 2017-18, services exceeded 50 percent, and the order was services greater than industry greater than agriculture.
accepted.tq: Combine historical shares and use the sector-order comparison.
accepted.sec: Sectoral share of GVA - at Independence vs now  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents sectoral growth in FY 2025-26?
accepted.x: The estimated sector growth rates for FY 2025-26 were agriculture 3.1 percent, industry 6.2 percent, manufacturing 7.0 percent and services 9.1 percent.
accepted.tq: Match each sector with its corresponding growth rate.
accepted.sec: Sectoral share of GVA - at Independence vs now  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the 2022-23 national accounts series, consider the following statements:
1. It raised agriculture's GVA by a range of 3.8 to 5.9 percent.
2. It reduced the measured trade GVA by 36 percent.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
accepted.x: The 2022-23 series raised agriculture's GVA by 3.8-5.9 percent and cut trade GVA by 36 percent.
accepted.tq: Test the paired upward and downward revisions together.
accepted.sec: Sectoral share of GVA - at Independence vs now  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly presents real GDP growth under the new series for 2022-23 and 2023-24?
accepted.x: Real GDP growth was 7.2 percent in 2022-23 and 7.2 percent in 2023-24 under the relevant figures of the new series. The older 2023-24 figure was 9.2 percent, while 8.2 percent was an earlier printed figure.
accepted.tq: Separate new-series figures from older and initially printed figures.
accepted.sec: Real GDP growth - recent years, trend, size since 1991  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The real GDP growth rate for 2024-25 under the new series was approximately:
accepted.x: Real GDP growth for 2024-25 was 7.1 percent under the new series; the old-series figure was 6.5 percent.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the revised figure from the old-series estimate.
accepted.sec: Real GDP growth - recent years, trend, size since 1991  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding real GDP growth in 2025-26:
1. The First Advance Estimate was 7.4 percent.
2. The Second Advance Estimate was 7.6 percent.
3. Q3 growth was 7.8 percent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The 2025-26 FAE was 7.4 percent, SAE was 7.6 percent and Q3 growth was 7.8 percent.
accepted.tq: Test closely related estimates by their sequence and labels.
accepted.sec: Real GDP growth - recent years, trend, size since 1991  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements best describes India's real GDP growth trend in the period covered?
o: It has remained unchanged at 7.2 percent since 2022-23.
It has increased steadily every year since 2020-21.
It has not followed a steady upward path because GDP contracted in 2020-21.
accepted.x: Growth did not rise steadily; the economy contracted in 2020-21, followed by subsequent recovery.
accepted.tq: Reject the absolute trend statement using the contraction exception.
accepted.sec: Real GDP growth - recent years, trend, size since 1991  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Since 1991, India's nominal GDP at market prices has increased approximately:
accepted.x: India's nominal GDP at market prices grew almost twelve times since 1991.
accepted.tq: Recall the long-period multiple rather than the annual growth rate.
accepted.sec: Real GDP growth - recent years, trend, size since 1991  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The approximate size of India's economy in 2025-26, according to the latest estimate cited, was:
accepted.x: The 2025-26 estimate placed the economy at about ₹345 lakh crore, equivalent to approximately USD 3.9 trillion.
accepted.tq: Match the rupee and dollar estimates as a pair.
accepted.sec: Real GDP growth - recent years, trend, size since 1991  [APPSC]

accepted.s: For States, per capita income is calculated as:
accepted.x: State per capita income is calculated as NSDP divided by population.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the national and State measures.
accepted.sec: Per capita income - formula, latest all-India figure, growth  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A comparison between per capita GSDP and per capita income is methodologically appropriate only when:
o: Gross measures are compared with gross measures and net measures with net measures.
Population is excluded from both measures.
A current-price measure is compared with a constant-price measure.
A gross measure is compared with a net measure.
accepted.x: Per capita GSDP is a gross measure, whereas per capita income is a net measure. Therefore, gross should be matched with gross and net with net.
accepted.tq: Apply the gross-versus-net distinction to a comparison problem.
accepted.sec: Per capita income - formula, latest all-India figure, growth  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The All-India per capita income at current prices for 2025-26 FAE was estimated at:
accepted.x: The All-India per capita income at current prices was estimated at ₹2,19,575 for 2025-26 FAE.
accepted.tq: Identify the latest estimate from closely spaced annual figures.
accepted.sec: Per capita income - formula, latest all-India figure, growth  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The increase in All-India per capita income in 2025-26 FAE over the preceding year was approximately:
accepted.x: All-India per capita income increased by 6.9 percent in 2025-26 FAE, compared with 8.7 percent in 2024-25 FRE.
accepted.tq: Separate the latest growth rate from the preceding year's rate.
accepted.sec: Per capita income - formula, latest all-India figure, growth  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The newer series placed average annual income per person at approximately:
accepted.x: The new series estimated average annual income per person at ₹2,43,180, or ₹20,265 per month.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the new-series average from current-price PCI estimates.
accepted.sec: Per capita income - formula, latest all-India figure, growth  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In which year did India's per capita income record its fastest growth among the years specified?
accepted.x: The fastest growth was recorded in 2021-22, at 18.6 percent, reflecting the post-COVID rebound.
accepted.tq: Link the peak growth rate with the post-COVID rebound.
accepted.sec: Per capita income - formula, latest all-India figure, growth  [APPSC]

accepted.s: India's per capita income declined by approximately what percentage in 2020-21?
accepted.x: Per capita income fell by 3.9 percent in 2020-21.
accepted.tq: Recall the contraction-year percentage.
accepted.sec: Per capita income - formula, latest all-India figure, growth  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Per capita income rises when:
o: Population grows faster than national income.
National income grows faster than population.
Population remains constant irrespective of national income.
Prices fall irrespective of income growth.
accepted.x: Per capita income rises when the growth of national income exceeds the growth of population.
accepted.tq: Apply the numerator-denominator relationship in the PCI formula.
accepted.sec: Per capita income - formula, latest all-India figure, growth  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly matches the 2025-26 FAE per capita figures?
accepted.x: For 2025-26 FAE, Andhra Pradesh PCI was ₹2,94,507 and All-India PCI was ₹2,19,575.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure year and match State and national values.
accepted.sec: Per capita income - formula, latest all-India figure, growth  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is a major explanation for the slow growth of per capita income?
o: Population growth, low productivity and a low-income, low-saving vicious circle
accepted.x: Population growth, low productivity and the low-income, low-saving vicious circle contribute to slow PCI growth.
accepted.tq: Identify the combined causal explanation rather than a single factor.
accepted.sec: Per capita income - formula, latest all-India figure, growth  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following States or Union Territories is included among those whose per capita incomes exceed the World Bank upper-middle-income threshold of USD 4,636?
accepted.x: Karnataka, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat and Delhi were identified as exceeding the USD 4,636 threshold.
accepted.tq: Use membership in the specified high-income group.
accepted.sec: Inter-state comparison - highest/lowest PCI, largest economies, AP rank  [APPSC]

accepted.s: India's per capita income in the comparison cited was approximately:
accepted.x: India as a whole had a per capita income of approximately USD 2,760 in the cited comparison.
accepted.tq: Separate India's average from the upper-middle-income threshold.
accepted.sec: Inter-state comparison - highest/lowest PCI, largest economies, AP rank  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the growth of State income groups since 1994-95:
1. Middle-income States grew 36.7 times.
2. The richest States grew 28.3 times.
3. The poorest States grew 26.6 times.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three growth multiples are correct: 36.7 times for middle-income States, 28.3 times for the richest States and 26.6 times for the poorest States.
accepted.tq: Test all three comparison-group multiples together.
accepted.sec: Inter-state comparison - highest/lowest PCI, largest economies, AP rank  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the 16th Finance Commission is correct?
o: It replaced income distance entirely with population density and reduced devolution to 25 percent.
It introduced a contribution criterion based on the square root of GSDP, while retaining the income-distance criterion and 41 percent devolution.
It based all devolution exclusively on per capita income and raised the share to 50 percent.
It removed the GSDP-based criterion and retained only the tax-effort criterion.
accepted.x: The new contribution criterion uses the square root of GSDP; the per capita GSDP income-distance criterion remains, and devolution remains at 41 percent.
accepted.tq: Identify the retained provisions alongside the new criterion.
accepted.sec: Inter-state comparison - highest/lowest PCI, largest economies, AP rank  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Andhra Pradesh ranked what position in India by GSDP, with its 2025-26 current-price GSDP estimated at ₹17.62 lakh crore?
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh ranked eighth by GSDP, with a 2025-26 current-price GSDP of ₹17.62 lakh crore.
accepted.tq: Match the State rank with its corresponding GSDP figure.
accepted.sec: Inter-state comparison - highest/lowest PCI, largest economies, AP rank  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly compares the 2025-26 current-price GSDP growth figures of Andhra Pradesh and India?
accepted.x: In 2025-26, Andhra Pradesh GSDP grew by 10.75 percent at current prices, compared with 8.0 percent for India.
accepted.tq: Avoid reversing the State and national comparison.
accepted.sec: Inter-state comparison - highest/lowest PCI, largest economies, AP rank  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In 2024-25, the constant-price GSDP growth of Andhra Pradesh and India was respectively:
accepted.x: In 2024-25, Andhra Pradesh recorded 9.24 percent constant-price GSDP growth, while India's growth was 6.4 percent.
accepted.tq: Keep current-price and constant-price comparisons separate.
accepted.sec: Inter-state comparison - highest/lowest PCI, largest economies, AP rank  [APPSC]

accepted.s: India's rank in the world by nominal GDP, after overtaking Japan in 2025 at USD 4.18 trillion, was:
accepted.x: India ranked fourth by nominal GDP after overtaking Japan in 2025, when its nominal GDP was stated as USD 4.18 trillion.
accepted.tq: Distinguish nominal ranking from PPP ranking.
accepted.sec: India's GDP rank - nominal and PPP, IMF projections, USD 5 trillion  [APPSC]

accepted.s: India's rank by GDP measured in purchasing power parity was:
o: 3rd, after the United States and China
accepted.x: India was the third-largest economy by PPP, after China and the United States.
accepted.tq: Use the ordering of economies under PPP rather than nominal GDP.
accepted.sec: India's GDP rank - nominal and PPP, IMF projections, USD 5 trillion  [APPSC]

accepted.s: India was projected to become the third-largest economy by:
accepted.x: India was projected to become the third-largest economy by 2028.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the projected ranking year from the income-classification year.
accepted.sec: India's GDP rank - nominal and PPP, IMF projections, USD 5 trillion  [APPSC]

accepted.s: India was projected to attain upper-middle-income status by:
accepted.x: The projection placed India's transition to upper-middle-income status by 2030.
accepted.tq: Separate the income-status milestone from the GDP-ranking milestone.
accepted.sec: India's GDP rank - nominal and PPP, IMF projections, USD 5 trillion  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes India's income classification in the cited World Bank classification?
o: High-income economy based on Atlas-method GNI per capita
Upper-middle-income economy based on nominal GDP
Lower-middle-income economy based on GNI per capita under the Atlas method
Low-income economy based on PPP GDP
accepted.x: India remained a lower-middle-income economy according to the World Bank's GNI per capita classification using the Atlas method. Classifications are updated each 1 July.
accepted.tq: Identify the authority, indicator and method used for classification.
accepted.sec: India's GDP rank - nominal and PPP, IMF projections, USD 5 trillion  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which institution implements the International Comparison Programme, with the National Statistical Office serving as the nodal agency in India?
accepted.x: The World Bank implements the ICP, while UNSD is associated with the programme and the NSO is the nodal agency in India.
accepted.tq: Use the institutional-role distinction rather than the programme name alone.
accepted.sec: India's GDP rank - nominal and PPP, IMF projections, USD 5 trillion  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which statement about India's position in the Asia-Pacific region by PPP is correct?
o: India is fourth in Asia-Pacific and fourth globally.
India is first in Asia-Pacific and third globally.
India is third in Asia-Pacific and second globally.
India is second in Asia-Pacific and third globally.
accepted.x: By PPP, India was the third-largest economy globally and the second-largest in the Asia-Pacific region.
accepted.tq: Keep regional and global ranks distinct.
accepted.sec: India's GDP rank - nominal and PPP, IMF projections, USD 5 trillion  [APPSC]
